decisions.quote: Although the threefold interaction between Response location, Time shift direction, and Shift magnitude on RT was not signiﬁcant in our study, our results largely replicate those of Sell and Kaschak (2011).
decisions.reason: Under Rule 1 and the codebook's 'mixed' definition, a component-level contrast ('In contrast to the original study, this congruency effect was not significantly modulated by the magnitude of time shift') is outweighed when the authors state a genuine overall verdict speaking to the replication as a whole. In both the Abstract and Discussion, the authors do not merely assert confirmation of the focal two-way congruency effect before reporting a contrast; rather, after reviewing the non-significant by-participant three-way interaction alongside the significant by-item three-way interaction, the matching qualitative pattern in Figure 1, and the separate simple-interaction analyses showing a significant congruency effect for large but not small time shifts, they issue an explicit post-contrast synthesis covering 'our results' as a whole: 'Although the threefold interaction ... was not significant in our study, our results largely replicate those of Sell and Kaschak (2011). Therefore, the present replication enforces the conclusion of the original study...' (mirroring the Abstract's 'In sum, this replication reinforces the basic conclusion by Sell and Kaschak... especially when the time shift is large'). Here 'largely replicate' functions as an overall affirmative replication verdict that explicitly subordinates the single non-significant omnibus interaction rather than framing the replication outcome as mixed.

scope_review.parent_objection: The discussion says: Although the threefold interaction ... was not significant in our study, our results largely replicate those of Sell and Kaschak (2011). Is this a genuine overall verdict under Rule 1, or only a focal-effect assertion? The first reply uses Rule 2 contrasting component results without settling the broad post-contrast verdict. Read abstract and full discussion, not just the three-way p-value. Decide under exact codebook priority: a genuine overall verdict outranks component contrasts; focal-effect confirmation does not. Explain scope of largely replicate rather than assume that partially successful or largely means either category automatically.

prior_reply.quote: We successfully replicated the basic congruency effect of the original study, that is, the interaction effect between direction of manual response and time reference when participants perform a sensicality judgment. In contrast to the original study, this congruency effect was not signiﬁcantly modulated by the magnitude of time shift.
prior_reply.reason: The paper re-tests two predictions from Sell and Kaschak (2011) Experiment 1—the two-way space-time congruency interaction and its three-way modulation by time-shift magnitude—and explicitly contrasts the non-significant modulation with the original study while qualifying its discussion summary ('Although the threefold interaction ... was not significant in our study, our results largely replicate those of Sell and Kaschak'). Under the codebook, a tested finding that the paper itself contrasts with the original ('in contrast to the original study') alongside a replicated effect makes the outcome mixed.
